headline: SILVER TOPS $82/OZ: Silver Miners Surge as US-Iran Ceasefire Hopes Ease Inflation Fears
snippet: Silver hit $82/oz on May 7 as hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire eased oil price and inflation concerns, sparking sharp gains across silver mining stocks. Endeavour Silver posted record Q1 silver sales of 1.64 million oz at an $85.95/oz realized price, with revenue up 230% year-over-year — underlining how brutally leveraged miners are to rising metals prices.

headline: COPPER HITS $6.24/LB RECORD: Strait of Hormuz Conflict Disrupts Sulphuric Acid Shipments
snippet: Copper reached $6.24/lb ($13,750/tonne) on May 8 — up 35.5% year-over-year — as the US-Iran Strait of Hormuz conflict disrupted sulphuric acid shipments, a key copper refining input. The supply shock collides with surging demand: continued data-centre buildouts are accelerating the long-run electrification case for the metal.

headline: SSR Mining SURGES 20%: Q1 Profit Triples as Average Realized Gold Hits $4,770/oz
snippet: SSR Mining (SSRM) rocketed 20% on May 6 after Q1 2026 EPS nearly tripled year-over-year to $1.15/share on an average realized gold price of $4,770/oz — up from $2,935/oz a year ago. The company ended Q1 debt-free with $634M cash after completing the $1.5B sale of its fire-damaged Copler mine interest, leaving it anchored by two major U.S. gold operations.

headline: SECOND-BEST INTERSECTION EVER: Power Metallic Drills 22m at 11.46% CuEq at Lion Zone
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) reported hole PML-26-095 cut 22 metres grading 11.46% copper-equivalent — the project's second-best intersection to date — with internal highs reaching 18.62% CuEq. The company is advancing toward an inaugural Mineral Resource Estimate in Q3 2026, and notes that Lion Zone grades consistently exceed average producing copper mine grades by more than an order of magnitude.

headline: Gold at $4,750 — Analysts Tell CNBC Bull Market Will Resume 'AS FOG OF WAR LIFTS'
snippet: Gold jumped 1.2% to $4,750/oz on May 7 as US-Iran ceasefire signals weighed on oil prices and lifted risk appetite, while market watchers told CNBC the historic precious metals rally is merely pausing. Analysts argue that the secular drivers — central bank buying, dollar erosion, geopolitical uncertainty — remain firmly intact, and any de-escalation is a buying opportunity rather than a peak.

headline: USGS Maps 2.33 Million Tonnes of Appalachian Lithium — U.S. Permitting Could Take 29 Years
snippet: A new USGS survey estimates 2.33 million metric tonnes of extractable lithium beneath multiple Appalachian states — a find that could rival known global reserves. The catch: the U.S. has the world's second-longest mine-permitting timeline at 29 years, raising questions about whether the discovery can be turned into strategic supply before China cements its battery metals dominance.

headline: AUSTRALIA-JAPAN Sign A$1.67B Critical Minerals Pact Targeting Rare Earths, Nickel, and Gallium
snippet: Australia and Japan signed a joint declaration on May 4 committing A$1.67B in combined government support to diversify critical minerals supply chains away from China. Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi are key co-investors; priority projects include Lynas Rare Earths, the Alcoa Gallium Recovery Project, and the Ardea Resources Kalgoorlie Nickel Project.

headline: CHINA Imported 790+ Tonnes of Silver in Early 2026 as Solar Boom Widens the Structural Deficit
snippet: US Global Investors' Gold SWOT report highlights China importing over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, driven primarily by its solar panel manufacturing boom. The structural silver deficit reached 148.9 million ounces in 2025 and shows no sign of narrowing — a key argument for silver's long-term bull case regardless of short-term price volatility from the Gulf conflict.

headline: Standard Uranium Locks In Highest-Confidence-Ever Drill Targets at Davidson River for Summer Campaign
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND) confirmed drill targets at its Davidson River project in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin following completion of ExoSphere Multiphysics and machine-learning surveys. The 8,000–10,000m program focuses on the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird conductor corridors — structural trends related to NexGen's Arrow and Paladin's Triple R deposits — with two rigs mobilizing May 31.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Resets Lithium Demand: Morgan Stanley Sees 80,000-Tonne 2026 Deficit
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery storage demand — driven by AI data-centre power needs and China's power sector reforms — is rapidly eroding lithium's supply surplus. Morgan Stanley now forecasts an 80,000-tonne LCE deficit in 2026, a dramatic reversal from the 61,000-tonne surplus expected for 2025, and the shift is beginning to show up in lithium equity prices.

headline: Will the $2.8B USA Rare Earth–Serra Verde Deal BREAK CHINA'S Rare Earth Monopoly?
snippet: USA Rare Earth's April acquisition of Brazil's Serra Verde Group for $2.8B — combining the only U.S. rare earth mine with an operating Brazilian processor — is being analyzed as a potential inflection point in Western supply-chain independence. The Diplomat examines whether the deal can meaningfully challenge China's grip on NdPr oxide and heavy rare earth processing given regulatory and capital hurdles ahead.
